title: M3A Career Skills and First Impressions
author: C·E·L Mathayom

slides.title: What skills do you need for work?
slides.body: Let's find out.
slides.notes: Greet students. Ask: What skills do you need for a good job? What do you see in the picture?

slides.title: Why is this lesson important?
slides.body:
• These words help you talk about jobs and school.
  • You will need them at interviews.
  • They help you understand how people make a good impression.

slides.title: Think about work
slides.body:
What skills do you need for a good job? Talk to your partner.

Opinion — Reason — Evidence
slides.notes: Pairs discuss for 2 minutes. Elicit a few ideas: teamwork, communication, patience. Keep it brief.

slides.title: Let's check your word knowledge
slides.notes: Transition to vocabulary presentation. Say: These are words about career skills. We will learn nine of them.

slides.body:
/dɪˈsaɪsɪv/
decisive
A decisive leader makes quick choices. She decides before the team waits too long.
slides.notes: Click 1: show word. Click 2: show context. CCQ: If a manager is decisive, does she wait long to decide?

slides.body:
/kriˈeɪtɪv/
creative
Creative people think of new ideas. They find answers nobody else sees.
slides.notes: Click 1: show word. Click 2: show context. CCQ: Is a creative person good at making new things?

slides.body:
/ˈpeɪʃns/
patience
Teaching small children takes patience. You must wait and stay calm.
slides.notes: Click 1: show word. Click 2: show context. CCQ: If you have patience, do you get angry quickly?

slides.body:
/ˈnætʃrəl ˈliːdə/
natural leader
A natural leader guides the group. Everyone listens when she speaks.
slides.notes: Click 1: show word. Click 2: show context. CCQ: Is a natural leader someone people follow?

slides.body:
/tiːm ˈpleɪə/
team player
A team player helps the group win. He shares the work and supports others.
slides.notes: Click 1: show word. Click 2: show context. CCQ: Is a team player someone who works alone?

slides.body:
/ˌænəˈlɪtɪkl skɪlz/
analytical skills
Analytical skills help you solve problems. You study the facts and find the answer.
slides.notes: Click 1: show word. Click 2: show context. CCQ: Do analytical skills help you understand difficult situations?

slides.body:
/kəˌmjuːnɪˈkeɪʃn skɪlz/
communication skills
Good communication skills win interviews. You speak clearly and listen well.
slides.notes: Click 1: show word. Click 2: show context. CCQ: What is a communication skill? (speaking, listening)

slides.body:
/taɪm ˈmænɪdʒmənt skɪlz/
time management skills
Time management skills keep you on track. You finish tasks before the deadline.
slides.notes: Click 1: show word. Click 2: show context. CCQ: If you manage your time well, are you often late?

slides.body:
/ɡʊd ˈpiːpl skɪlz/
good people skills
Good people skills make you easy to work with. You stay friendly and calm with everyone.
slides.notes: Click 1: show word. Click 2: show context. CCQ: Does a person with good people skills get along with others?

slides.title: Interview at International School Bangkok
slides.notes: Transition to listening. Say: We will listen to an interview at an international school in Bangkok.

slides.title: Strategy: Predict
slides.body:
DoPredict what the director will ask.
WhyIt helps your brain focus.
HowRead the questions. Think first.
slides.notes: Say: The title is Interview at International School Bangkok. A director interviews a student. What might he ask? Predict first, then listen.

slides.title: Try it: Predict
slides.body:
A director interviews a new student.
Which topics might he ask about?
 Her favorite food.
 Her best skills.
 A movie she watched.
 Her plans for the future.
slides.notes: Ask students to predict which topics a director might ask about. Click to reveal the checkmarks.

slides.title: Try it: Predict
slides.body:
A director interviews a new student.
Which topics might he ask about?
 Her favorite food.
✓Her best skills.
 A movie she watched.
✓Her plans for the future.
slides.notes: Revealed: skills and future plans make sense. Food and movies are less likely for a school interview.

slides.body:
Listen — Gist

Why is Lily at International School Bangkok?
slides.notes: Play the dialog once. Students listen for the gist only: Why is Lily at the school?

slides.title: Gist — Answer
slides.body:
QuestionWhy is Lily at International School Bangkok?
AnswerShe is having an interview to join the school.
ExplanationThe director interviews her, and she hopes to get a place at the school.
Transcript“I really hope I get a place at your school.”
slides.notes: Confirm the gist. Lily is applying to join the international school.

slides.body:
Listen again

Answer the questions.

1. What does the director say about first impressions?

2. What is Lily's best skill?

3. What happened with the school play?

4. What does Lily need to work on?
slides.notes: Play the dialog again. Students answer the four detail questions. Then go through the answer slides.

slides.title: Answers (1/4)
slides.body:
Question1. What does the director say about first impressions?
AnswerThey start with a handshake. A good first impression matters.
ExplanationLily agrees and says she makes eye contact and smiles.
Transcript“We like to start with a handshake. A good first impression matters.”
slides.notes: Check the answer. Point out handshake, make eye contact from the unit.

slides.title: Answers (2/4)
slides.body:
Question2. What is Lily's best skill?
AnswerCommunication. She listens well and enjoys talking to people.
ExplanationShe also says she is a team player who stays calm under pressure.
Transcript“My best skill is communication. I listen well.”
slides.notes: Check the answer. Point out communication and team player from the vocabulary.

slides.title: Answers (3/4)
slides.body:
Question3. What happened with the school play?
AnswerIt lost its director. Lily came up with a new plan, and they acted out all the scenes in one week.
ExplanationSome friends dropped out, but she faced up to the challenge. Hard work pays off.
Transcript“I came up with a new plan, and we acted out all the scenes in one week.”
slides.notes: Check the answer. Point out the multi-word verbs: came up with, acted out, dropped out, faced up to, pays off.

slides.title: Answers (4/4)
slides.body:
Question4. What does Lily need to work on?
AnswerHer time management. She leaves big tasks to the last minute.
ExplanationThe director says patience helps and time management is a skill you can learn.
Transcript“I sometimes leave big tasks to the last minute.”
slides.notes: Check the answer. Point out time management and patience from the vocabulary.

slides.body:
Exercise 1 — Answers

Check your answers.

1Emma doesn't waste time – she always makes a decision and trusts her instincts. decisive
2Sara listens well and gets the best out of everyone. natural leader
3Li thinks of ideas that no one else thinks of. creative
4Ahmed understands processes and situations very well. analytical skills
5Felicity can express complicated ideas really clearly. communication skills
6Ramon works very well in groups. team player

8Dmitry stays calm when other people might get really angry. patience
9Jens never misses his deadlines – he's really organized. time management skills

slides.title: Exercise 5 — Page 124
slides.body:
Add the missing words.

Complete the travel guide.

Is the information true or false about your country?
slides.notes: Students complete Exercise 5 (first impressions travel guide). Then check the completed guide.

slides.body:
Exercise 5 — Answers

If you spend time in Bangkok, you should know about how people interact. Friends usually shake hands or kiss each other on the cheek when they meet.

When people make small talk, they usually chat about the weather or sports like basketball or soccer.

If you want to make a good impression, wearing smart clothes will impress people. But it's also important to smile and make eye contact.

If you don't look at people directly, they won't trust you.
slides.notes: The completed travel guide with all 5 answers. Each click reveals the next paragraph.

slides.title: Talk with your partner
slides.body:
Is the travel guide true about your country?

What is your best career skill?

OpinionI think first impressions matter a lot.
ReasonOne reason is people decide quickly.
EvidenceFor example, the director started with a handshake.

Opinion — Reason — Evidence
slides.notes: Pairs discuss. Use at least five target words: communication skills, team player, decisive, make eye contact, make small talk, patience... Pairs report one idea to the class.

slides.title: Quick round
slides.body: I say the meaning. You say the word.
slides.notes: Quick-fire retrieval: teacher says a definition, students say the word. Use the spelling test words. Say: These words will return in next lesson's warm-up. Exit question: Which word was most useful for you?
